samples.summary: Feature ships entirely inert: the version gate can never open on this build, so none of the doc's Goals are met for any user
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/package.json` pins `"@yorkie-js/react": "0.7.22"`, and `lib/yorkie-capabilities.ts` sets `MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"`. `supportsClientKey()` is the first term of `useDurableDocument`'s eligibility (`lib/use-durable-document.ts`), gates the Settings section (`app/settings/page.tsx`), and gates the chip's offer (`sync-status-chip.tsx`). So on the merged pin no document is ever durable, no opt-in is even visible, and `offline-local-persistence.md` § Goals ("Edits made while disconnected survive a reload or a browser crash") is unmet for every user. The doc declares this deliberately in § Rollout ("PR 4 lands inert, and stays inert until one upstream release... The Goals at the top of this document are unmet until the dependency is bumped"), which is why this is graded minor rather than major — nothing regresses and the safe direction is chosen. But it means several thousand lines of production code land unexercised in production, and a reviewer weighing this change should know the behaviour is not what is being validated here.

samples.summary: Preference module is a verbatim clone of `date-format-preference.ts` and the two have already diverged
samples.evidence: `lib/offline-persistence-preference.ts` reproduces `lib/date-format-preference.ts` line for line — same `STORAGE_KEY`/`CHANGE_EVENT` pair, same `memoryEnabled`/`memoryFormat` session mirror, same `subscribe`/`useSyncExternalStore` shape, and the explanatory comments are copied word for word ("Session-only copy of the preference, set *only* when persisting it failed", "The mirror is only non-null when the last write failed"). The repo expects reuse and keeps shared code in `@wafflebase/core`; a `createLocalPreference<T>(key, default, parse)` was the obvious extraction. This is the rubric's "duplicated logic that will now diverge" case and it is not hypothetical: the new copy adds a module-scope `storage` listener that retires the stale mirror when another tab changes the key (lines around the `if (typeof window !== "undefined")` block), and `date-format-preference.ts` has no equivalent — so the two modules now give different answers to the same question about mirror staleness. Graded minor because the divergent behaviour costs at most a stale date-format column in a rare private-browsing/second-tab path. The design doc says the preference is "built on `lib/date-format-preference.ts`'s shape", which is ambiguous between reuse and copy.

samples.summary: The `LocalChangesDropped` reason is discarded, so the recovery message cannot name "the three reasons" the design requires
samples.evidence: `offline-local-persistence.md` § Losing work anyway states: "The user is then told what happened, **in the vocabulary of the three reasons**, with a link to the copy" — naming `epoch-reanchor`, `document-purged`, `actor-mismatch`. The SDK event carries it (the durable-provider test fires `{ value: { reason: 'epoch-reanchor' } }`), but `DurableLossWatch`'s handler ignores the event payload entirely: it calls `durable.store.expectLoss(doc.getKey())` and `durable.reportLoss()` with no argument, and nothing on `DurableDocumentValue` (`lib/durable-document-context.ts`) or `ArchiveRecord` (`lib/wafflebase-doc-store.ts`) carries a reason field. The resulting toast in `offline-runtime.tsx` says only "Edits to \"<title>\" could not be reconciled with the server" — the same sentence for all three causes. The work is still returned, so the cost is limited to the user not learning why; but it is a stated user-facing requirement of the feature that is not implemented.

samples.summary: `documentIdsIn` re-derives a workspace's documents from a full cross-workspace listing instead of the scoped endpoint already in the same file
samples.evidence: `documentIdsIn` calls `fetchWorkspace(ref)` and then `fetchDocuments()` — the unscoped `GET /documents` — and filters client-side on `document.workspaceId`. `packages/frontend/src/api/workspaces.ts:290` already exports `fetchWorkspaceDocuments(workspaceId, folderId?)`, backed by `GET /workspaces/:id/documents`, in the very same module. The new helper therefore issues two requests (one of them a full listing of every document the user can read across every workspace) where one scoped request existed. There is a plausible reason not to reuse it — the docstring says "folders included", and `fetchWorkspaceDocuments` with no `folderId` lists the workspace root rather than recursing — but that reason is nowhere stated in the code, and it is the kind of unexplained near-duplication the repo's reuse expectation exists to prevent. If the recursion caveat is the reason, it belongs in the comment; if it is not, the existing endpoint should be used.

samples.summary: Design doc claims the recovery path reuses `DocumentCopyService` / `POST /documents/:id/copy`; it does not
samples.evidence: § Losing work anyway says "we already have the machinery for it in `DocumentCopyService` / `POST /documents/:id/copy`", and § See Also lists "[document-copy.md](document-copy.md) — the copy engine the offline-copy recovery path reuses". The implementation in `lib/offline-copy-recovery.ts` uses neither: it calls `createWorkspaceDocument(...)` followed by `applyImportedContent(...)` (the *import* engine), and for notes a bespoke `writeNote` that attaches its own client. Reusing the import engine is arguably the correct call — the copy endpoint duplicates an existing server-side document and cannot be fed archived bytes — but the doc now points a future reader at the wrong module, and the See Also link asserts a dependency that does not exist. Since the doc is the canonical record for this subsystem, it should name `apply-imported-content.ts` instead.

samples.summary: Design doc's "Layout and migration" describes a two-store schema and an `onupgradeneeded` migration that the implementation does not have
samples.evidence: The doc says "the database carries two object stores plus the per-entry metadata cleanup needs" and specifies a migration: "An `onupgradeneeded` that relocates each existing value into the snapshot store, with an empty change log beside it, is the whole migration." `lib/wafflebase-doc-store.ts` creates **four** object stores (`snapshots`, `headers`, `changes`, `archives`) and performs no relocation at all — its `onupgradeneeded` comment reads "Version 1 creates; there is nothing in the wild to migrate. No wafflebase build has ever passed `ClientOptions.store`, so no browser holds an older layout." That reasoning is sound and probably supersedes the doc's paragraph, but the doc was not updated to match, so the canonical record describes a schema and a migration path that do not exist.

samples.summary: `keepArchives` is dead API whose justifying comment names a caller the final design removed
samples.evidence: `WafflebaseDocStore.dropAllForUser(userId, { keepArchives })` and `eraseOfflineData(store, userId, { keepArchives })` both thread the option, and the store's comment explains it as "for the one caller that did not ask for any of this: a session the server expired". But the final design reversed that: `offline-local-persistence.md`'s cleanup table now reads "Session expired (401) | Nothing. A live entry carries the un-pushed change log, and nobody asked", and `api/auth.ts` implements it by passing `eraseLocalData: "none"` so no erase runs at all on 401. A grep across the repo finds no caller that ever passes `keepArchives`. The result is an unused option on two public functions carrying a rationale that contradicts the shipped design — a maintenance trap for whoever reads it next.

samples.summary: The README index row for `sync-status.md` is now stale — it still states offline persistence is deferred and that the wording never claims local durability
samples.evidence: The diff adds a new row for `offline-local-persistence.md` but leaves the adjacent `sync-status.md` row unchanged, and it still reads: "Offline persistence deferred — `@yorkie-js/sdk@0.7.20` added an opt-in `ClientOptions.store` but we pass none, and turning it on needs a stable `clientKey`, which activates the SDK's single-active-session guard and costs the second tab on an open document — which is why the wording never claims local durability". Every clause of that is now superseded by this change: `sync-status.md` itself was revised in this diff to strike the Non-Goal, a store *is* passed on the durable path, the second-tab cost is handled by the app-owned election, and the chip's new `saved-locally` state does claim local durability. `docs/design/README.md` is the index CONTRIBUTING requires docs to be registered in, so a row that contradicts the document it summarises is a real doc-discipline defect, even though nothing behavioural depends on it.

samples.summary: The doc's own staged rollout (PRs 2–5, landing separately) is collapsed into a single change
samples.evidence: § Rollout tabulates PR 2 (`WafflebaseDocStore`, "**not yet wired**, so it is pure addition and independently testable"), PR 3 ("Per-document client, app lock, fallback — **still passing no store**. Structure only"), PR 4 (wire the store, Settings + chip opt-in, `durable`, unload guard, toast, recovery) and PR 5 (revise `sync-status.md`), and justifies the split explicitly: "The structural change and the behavior change land separately, so that a regression in either is unambiguous." This diff contains all four at once — the store, the per-document client and lock, the wiring plus both opt-in surfaces, and the `sync-status.md` revision. The cost is reviewability rather than anything a user sees, and I cannot see upstream PR boundaries from the diff alone (this may be a squashed view of four merged PRs), hence medium confidence. If it genuinely landed as one change, the doc's rollout section should be amended to say so rather than left describing a plan that was not followed.

samples.summary: `writeNote` re-implements the Yorkie client attach/seed lifecycle instead of extending the import engine it sits beside
samples.evidence: `writeNote` constructs its own `new Client({ rpcAddr, apiKey, authTokenInjector: fetchYorkieToken })`, activates, attaches a `note-<id>` document, seeds `root.content`, detaches and deactivates. `app/documents/apply-imported-content.ts` already owns exactly that lifecycle for the four engine types (its own comment here acknowledges the mirroring: "Mirrors `applyImportedContent`'s own lifecycle: `activate()` sits outside the `try`..."). The stated reason — a note is one Yorkie `Text` rather than an engine document, so `ImportedContent` has no branch for it — is legitimate, but it argues for adding a `note` arm to `ImportedContent`/`applyImportedContent` rather than for a second client-lifecycle implementation in a different module. Two copies of the activate/attach/detach/deactivate dance will drift when the client options change (e.g. if a future change adds `metadata` or a retry policy to the import path).

samples.summary: A vitest suite lives in production source under a non-test filename
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/lib/doc-store-contract.ts` imports `describe, it, expect` from `vitest` and exports `testDocStoreContract`, but is named as an ordinary source module in `src/lib/` rather than `*.test.ts` or a `__tests__`/test-support directory. It is only imported from `wafflebase-doc-store.test.ts`, so nothing pulls vitest into the app bundle today, but the placement makes that one careless import away. The file's own rationale for existing (a transcription of the SDK's unpublished contract suite, run against both `MemoryDocStore` and ours) is good and I am not disputing the approach — only where it sits.

samples.summary: Unrelated whole-file formatting churn is mixed into a feature change
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/vite.config.ts` is rewritten from double to single quotes across ~80 lines with no functional change other than the two `__YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__` additions; `src/lib/utils.ts` changes only to add semicolons; `components/__tests__/collab-document-provider.test.tsx` is requoted throughout for two real mock additions; `sync-status-chip.tsx` reflows the tooltip import. Prettier is write-only in this repo and no lane checks formatting, so none of this is required by CI — it is pure diff noise that makes the substantive changes in those files harder to find. Worth splitting out or reverting.

mergedFrom.summary: The offline-transition toast promised for the durable case is absent. offline-local-persistence.md:489 lists two consequences that "follow automatically": the `beforeunload` guard is suppressed when durable (implemented — `mayHaveUnsent` is false in `saved-locally`), "and the offline-transition toast changes from 'keep this tab open' to 'saved to this device'". The toast effect keys on `stranded`, i.e. `state === 'not-saved'` only, so a durable document going offline emits no toast at all rather

finding.summary: The chip's offline call-to-action fires on the share-link route the design excludes, promising persistence that can never happen there. `offerOffline = stranded && supportsClientKey() && !offlineEnabled` consults neither the identity nor the `not-permitted` lapse. `SharedHeaderStatus` (shared-header-status.tsx:26) renders `SyncStatusChip` for every editor-role share-link visitor, and `shared-document.tsx` wraps the route in `NonDurableScope`, so this document can never be durable. An anonymous visitor who strands work gets the chip rendered as a button plus a toast action, and clicking it emits `toast.success('Saving on this device is on', … 'Documents you open from now on keep un-sent changes on this device')` — false for a visitor with no account, and false for this document in every case. This contradicts the design twice: "Anonymous share-link editors" is a stated Non-Goal (offline-local-persistence.md:64), and sync-status-tooltip.ts:31-34 already withholds the `not-permitted` explanation on the reasoning that saying so "would describe the feature to somebody who does not have it" — the button says it far more loudly. It also cuts against the Goal "the sync chip tells the truth about durability in every case" (line 52). Cost: a user told their unsent work is now kept when nothing is keeping it, on the one route the design decided not to persist.

verdict.reason: The finding's central evidence is not what the file contains. `sync-status-chip.tsx:94-98` defines `offerOffline = stranded && supportsClientKey() && !offlineEnabled && lapse !== 'not-permitted'` — the `not-permitted` term the finding says is missing is present, fed by `useDurabilityLapse()` at line 78, and documented at lines 86-93 with the exact Non-Goal reasoning the finding cites. The guard is live on the route named: `shared-document.tsx:1016` wraps the share route in `NonDurableScope`; `collab-document-provider.tsx:218,291-299,350` reads `useDurabilityPermitted()` and publishes `lapse = "not-permitted"` through a `DurabilityLapseScope` that wraps both branches; `app/shared/shared-header-status.tsx:26` renders `SyncStatusChip` inside those layouts, hence inside that scope. So neither the button branch (line 273) nor the toast `action` (line 217) can render for a share-link visitor, and the claimed false 'Saving on this device is on' toast is unreachable there. Tests at tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx:588-609 assert the suppression and its control case. The identity check is genuinely absent, but anonymous editors reach an editor only via the share-link route, which this lapse already covers, so no user-facing cost remains.

finding.summary: Swallowing a failed `doc.subscribe` leaves `durable` true, breaking the design's "durable ⇒ reportable" / under-promise rule — and, for the loss event, also breaks archive-on-remove
finding.evidence: The new `watch()` helper catches a throwing `subscribe` and only `console.warn`s; nothing flips the durability state. `docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md` states the invariant explicitly: "Durable-but-unreportable is worse than uniformly non-durable: it is a guarantee the user cannot see, check, or be warned about when it lapses" (§ Who gets it) and "A failure the store cannot classify still flips `durable` — the default is to under-promise" (§ What the user sees). After a swallowed failure the chip keeps reading `Saved to this device` for a document whose `PersistDisabled`/`LocalChangesDropped` can never be reported. Worse, the comment's claim that this "costs the chip its certainty, never the document" does not hold for the first subscription: per § Storage, `WafflebaseDocStore.remove()` archives only what `expectLoss` latched (`wafflebase-doc-store.ts:739,757`), and the SDK calls `remove` on every detach — so if the `local-changes-dropped` subscription silently fails, unreconciled work is deleted instead of archived, defeating the Goal "Work that genuinely cannot be reconciled with the server is returned to the user as a document." The safe shape the design asks for is to latch durability off (a lapse reason) when a required durability event cannot be watched, rather than to continue silently.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the `watch()` helper swallows a throwing `doc.subscribe` with only a `console.warn` and never flips durability state. The code in the working tree does not match that description. `watch()` returns a boolean (`durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:295-306`: `return true` on success, `return false` in the catch), and both call sites consume it. On loss-subscription failure (`:314-332`) it latches `durable.store.expectLoss(doc.getKey())` inside a guarded try (`:324-328`) AND calls `durable.reportUnreportable()` (`:331`); on persist-disabled failure (`:344-349`) it calls `durable.reportUnreportable()` (`:348`). `reportUnreportable` sets the `unreportable` state (`:143-144`), which is a conjunct of the published value `durable: !lost && !writesFailing && !persistDisabled && !unreportable` (`:194`) and yields the distinct lapse reason `'unreportable'` (`:224`), declared at `durable-document-context.ts:121-122` and surfaced in the tooltip at `sync-status-tooltip.ts:38`. The context contract documents this rule quoting the same design sentence the finding cites (`durable-document-context.ts:40-51`). The secondary archive-on-remove consequence also does not follow: `remove()` archives when the latch is set (`wafflebase-doc-store.ts:809`, `777-779`), and the failure branch sets that latch precisely so an unobservable loss archives rather than deletes. The remedy the finding asks for ("latch durability off with a lapse reason when a required durability event cannot be watched") is what the code already implements; the finding appears to describe an earlier revision.
